text:
Alex: heads-up from the canary this morning — saw a bunch of Triton->CUTLASS fallbacks on the kv-hot path around seq_len ~ 1200. p95 jumped ~2.4x for affected requests.

Maria: ouch. any obvious trigger? model, batch size, or just seqlen ramp?

Alex: looks correlated with KV cache hits + large prefix lengths. pattern: small batches (1-4) but seqlen > 1k, Triton chooses a slow path, then runtime decides to fallback to CUTLASS which sometimes saturates and adds queuing.

Tyler: do we have profiler traces? can we get the kernel decision logs?

Alex: uploaded sample trace to perf-bot, here are the snippets from runtime-decider: 
```
[decision] model: llama-70b, device: h100, batch: 2, seqlen: 1216 -> chosen: triton_ff
[fallback] reason: kernel_unstable_latency, metric: 1.9ms->4.7ms
[probe] sample_ratio=0.02, recent_win=10m, fallback_count=8
```

perf-bot: uploaded trace: https://internal.perf/trace/1831234567 (access: eng-runtime) :rotating_light:

Samir: I think the probe sample is too sparse on the kv-hot path. When KV hits happen you get very different memory access patterns — the kernel perf distribution has a long tail. small sample_ratio misses the tail and then fallback oscillates.

Maria: agreed. also the current hysteresis is symmetric; if fallback triggers we flip immediately and then flip back after a single successful probe. that will oscillate with bursty KV cache locality.

Tyler: proposed tweak: decouple probe sampling for kv-hotpath and increase sample_ratio to 0.1 for seqlen>1024, add asymmetry to hysteresis (min_stable=3 successful probes to switch back).

Alex: tried that locally with canary config: 
```
routing:
  kv_hotpath:
    seqlen_threshold: 1024
    probe_ratio_high_seqlen: 0.1
    fallback_hysteresis:
      min_down: 2
      min_up: 3
```
Result: fallback rate dropped 75%, p95 improved to within 1.15x baseline. small regression on p50 for some tiny batches (~+3%).

Samir: promising. but watch out for cost: CUTLASS uses more SMs in some kernels, so if probing too often we may increase GPU utilization. Did you check utilization/cost?

Alex: yes, GPU util increased ~6% during probe spikes — still under threshold for canary fleet. but if we roll to dedicated pools we should gate by tenant tier or add rate cap.

Maria: another angle: for kv-hotpath we could add a sequence-length-aware kernel hint from the compiler stage. if model.onnx metadata includes "kv_hot=true" and avg_prefix>512 we could bias routing at request admission time, avoid runtime probe overhead.

Tyler: that requires model onboarding changes and metadata sharing across runtime. doable but longer lead time. quick win is runtime config change + better metrics.

Samir: also, KV cache can change effective seqlen (kv hits reduce compute but increase memory ops). we should log "effective_mem_bandwidth" estimate into traces so the decider can use a second feature beyond seqlen.

Alex: added a quick patch to trace: emit kv_hit_ratio and est_mem_bw. replayed traces match our hypothesis: high kv_hit_ratio + high est_mem_bw correlates with Triton instability.

perf-bot: experiment metrics (canary): fallback_count reduced from 42->10 (24h), p95 latency down from 420ms->290ms for the cohort, GPU util +6%. Link: https://internal.perf/exp/1831234567-results

Maria: next steps?

Alex: 1) apply probe_ratio increase and hysteresis tweak to canary fleet (in progress). 2) add kv_hit_ratio/est_mem_bw to routing features (Samir + Tyler). 3) draft rollout plan with tier gating and cost cap (me + Maria).

Tyler: I'll open the PR for the runtime decider change and add tests for oscillation (simulate bursts).

Samir: I'll add the mem-bandwidth estimator to trace library and run offline eval on last 7d of traces.

Maria: create a short postmortem note in #postmortems once we confirm rollout. add an alert for fallback_rate > 5% on any fleet.

Alex: thanks team. tagging @eng-sre to watch canary during rollout. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: alert created: fallback_rate alert on canary (threshold 5%)
